<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getObject (symbol, a method of interface ParentCodeFieldRegistry))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via /object/:name/state/:field (route, bridged from symbol getObject — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via getLegalNextStates (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field; the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field), meta.getLegalNextStates (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via getLegalNextStates (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field; the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field), meta.getLegalNextStates (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 240e9ab597a9b9a2dc3f46fe0d4432b3030b5de9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3bce20731e1d9d87de8f0c19d6d9f83e80380fd8` — the merge of head `d50cea4559b540e3bc7aa7ee10e2d33f2171fe97` into base `240e9ab597a9b9a2dc3f46fe0d4432b3030b5de9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3bce20731e1d9d87de8f0c19d6d9f83e80380fd8 && git checkout 3bce20731e1d9d87de8f0c19d6d9f83e80380fd8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 240e9ab597a9b9a2dc3f46fe0d4432b3030b5de9 d50cea4559b540e3bc7aa7ee10e2d33f2171fe97 && git checkout -B drift-repro 240e9ab597a9b9a2dc3f46fe0d4432b3030b5de9 && git merge --no-ff d50cea4559b540e3bc7aa7ee10e2d33f2171fe97

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 240e9ab597a9b9a2dc3f46fe0d4432b3030b5de9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 240e9ab597a9b9a2dc3f46fe0d4432b3030b5de9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `d50cea4559b540e3bc7aa7ee10e2d33f2171fe97`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T17:17Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `0ac112fc` (6 files, +207/−35, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

**What holds**

- **Scope and declaration.** Only the refusal's text changes. `ERR_CURRENCY_CODE_REQUIRED`/400, `field`, `fields` and `amountField` are unchanged, and the error-code ledger records the code and status, not the text. No export from the package entry moves, so `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` hold, and an `@objectstack/objectql` patch is right. The diff touches no contract face, so no contract record is owed.
- **No new read on the accepted path.** `assertRecordCurrencyCodes` asks the new `parentCodeServing` reader only after `hits` is non-empty, and only about the first hit's parent. It asks only when that pair follows a parent (`path.master` set). The reader makes registry metadata reads only (`getObject`, `getObjectContributors`, `isPackageDisabled`), with no data read.
- **The new branch is narrow and fails toward today's text.** It fires only when the parent object is served and its served field map lacks the code field. A parent that is not served at all (`getObject` undefined) keeps today's text, as the PR says. So does any lookup that misses for another reason. The package clause names only disabled contributors whose own definition still declares the field. Otherwise it gives the card's generic clause, which matches the registry's behaviour: a disable keeps the `extend` contribution and an uninstall removes it.
- **The constructor refactor is byte-preserving.** `codeRequiredMessage` reproduces the old composition for every other branch. The CONTROL pins the full blank-code text with `toBe`.
- **Every write door is wired.** The four write-side callers pass the reader: insert, by-id update, predicate update and the `validate()` preview.
- **Tests.** The disable path and then the uninstall path run on a real registry fixture. Each asserts the envelope, the `field`, the clause, the absence of "has a blank" and that no row was written. I accept the ablation of the reader call as reported: the disable test goes red and the CONTROL stays green.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

1. Only the insert door is pinned. A by-id or predicate update that dropped the new argument would quietly fall back to the old text, and nothing would go red. A one-line update pin on the same fixture would close that. Fold it into a later card on this guard.
2. The new clause tells any writer of the child object the id of a disabled package. That is metadata of the same kind the message already names (objects, fields, the master_detail), so I see no new exposure. I am noting it in case the platform later decides package ids are admin-only.

**Gates:** at review time 35 success, 16 skipped, none red, so every check is green.
